question.text: The decay constant for a radioactive nuclide is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Atomic weight of the substance is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mole</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>23</mn></msup></math>. The activity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mo>µ</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of the substance is ________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>10</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Bq</mi></math>.

solution.text:
It is given that 

λ=1.5×10-5 s-1

Number of moles is 1×10-660=10-76

Number of atoms=number of moles ×NA

N0=10-76×6×1023=1016

Hence, at t=0, A=A0=N0λ, the activity can be given by

A=N0λe-λt⇒A=1016×1.5×10-5×1=15×1010 Bq
